drills.q: New event-driven service on Azure Functions in 2026: which plan and why?
drills.a: Flex Consumption - GA Nov 2024, scale-to-zero, fast per-concurrency scaling, VNet integration, per-function scaling groups, up to 1000 instances; legacy Consumption is deprecated-track.

drills.q: Client HTTP calls time out at exactly ~4 minutes despite 10-minute functionTimeout. Explain.
drills.a: ~230 s Azure Load Balancer idle timeout caps HTTP responses regardless of config; return 202 Accepted with a Durable status URL instead of extending timeouts.

drills.q: Orchestrations produce duplicate charges after scale-out. Diagnose.
drills.a: Non-deterministic code (wall-clock/random/direct I/O) replayed divergently or non-idempotent activities retried. Enforce determinism, context-provided time, idempotency keys on payment activities; version orchestrators when fixing history.

drills.q: Queue messages vanish without errors logged. Where did they go?
drills.a: Poison queue: moved to <queue>-poison after MaxDequeueCount=5 failed attempts. Alert on poison depth, add handler, keep processing idempotent (at-least-once delivery).

drills.q: Bill tripled after moving off Consumption to Premium to kill cold starts. Why?
drills.a: Premium bills continuous core-seconds with >=1 always-billed instance and no execution charges; for spiky low-traffic apps the floor dominates. Use Flex always-ready sized to baseline instead of whole-plan Premium.

drills.q: Design a nightly 50k-row pipeline with per-tenant emails using Functions.
drills.a: Durable fan-out/fan-in: starter fetches count, chunk into ~500-row activity batches with retry options, aggregate incrementally via entity to bound fan-in memory, emails as final activities. Move task hub to Durable Task Scheduler if throughput high.

drills.q: An LLM agent loop (minutes-long multi-step turns) is proposed as a plain HTTP-triggered Function. Critique.
drills.a: Wrong twice: synchronous HTTP hits ~230 s ceiling and cold starts mid-loop; crash at step 7/10 loses paid progress. Use Durable orchestrator per turn (tool calls = activities, poll status URL) or Container Apps with externalized state.

drills.q: After migrating Consumption to Flex, the downstream database starts timing out. What changed?
drills.a: Concurrency multiplication: N instances x C concurrent requests now hit dependencies simultaneously. Cap maximumInstanceCount x concurrency below the DB connection budget; note Python defaults C=1 until set.

drills.q: What do you give up choosing Flex Consumption over Premium?
drills.a: Windows runtimes, deployment slots (replaced by traffic-weighted site update strategies), PowerShell managed dependencies, polling blob triggers (Event Grid only); one app per plan.

drills.q: Rank by incident frequency: cold starts, poison queues, non-deterministic orchestrators, connection exhaustion.
drills.a: 1 connection exhaustion (silent growth), 2 poison queues (constant silent loss), 3 non-deterministic orchestrators (rare but catastrophic), 4 cold starts (annoyance once mitigated) - inverts how often each gets discussed.
